newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares close sharply up as strike fears ease.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares close sharply up as strike fears ease.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed sharply higher on Tuesday after a weak response to all-out strike calls and increasing fund inflows boosted sentiment, brokers said.
Blue-chip manufacturing stocks, which stood to be major casualties from the strikes, soared to close at daily limits.
The composite index climbed 4.1 percent, or 27.05 points, to a provisional close at 686.59. Advancing stocks eclipsed decliners, 769 to 81.

"Buying was very strong. This is something we hardly expected earlier," said Lim Chong-woo of Ssangyong Investment and Securities. "I think this strength could hold on further, directly breaking through the symbolic 700-point mark soon."
Fears over what was expected to be the worst strike ever quickly eased as buses and commuter trains were running almost on time in the capital, brokers said.

Blue-chip Samsung Electronics rose to its daily limit to close at 47,500 won by gaining 3,500. Hyundai Motor Co, one of the major casualties from the strikes, also closed at its upper limit of 24,500 won by adding 1,800.
South Korea limits daily movement of each stock's price at eight percent up or down from the previous close.
Trade volume totalled 36.55 million shares, sharply up from Monday's 28.73 million.
Brokers also said sentiment was boosted because customer deposits were outpacing outstanding loans used for margin trading for the first time in three months.
"It's a really big boost and now supports hopes that the market has taken off for a major rebound," Park Byung-moon, head of sales at LG Securities, said.
